title: Route the Batch at the Fork
subtitle: Auto-approve the clean invoice, send the rest to exceptions
scenario: It is 11:30 AM at the fork. Every invoice now carries its checks - duplicate flag, match result, vendor status, receipt status. Route each one: only the invoice that is clean on every count auto-approves; each of the others goes to the exception queue with the reason it failed.
input: INV-59001: not duplicate, within tolerance, qty match, vendor on file, receipt present. INV-59002: within all but price is over tolerance (variance 90 > band 25). INV-58962: duplicate (already paid day-0). INV-59004: vendor V-1205 not in master. INV-59005: price within tolerance but no receipt (two-way only). Rule: auto-approve only if not duplicate AND within tolerance AND qty match AND vendor on file; otherwise exception.
instructions: For each invoice, apply the routing rule to its checks.
Set route to auto-approve only for the fully clean invoice; exception for the rest.
Set reason: clean match, price over tolerance, duplicate, vendor not in master, or missing receipt.
Remember a duplicate always wins - it routes to exception regardless of its other checks.
Return a JSON array of the five rows, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Route five invoices at the match fork. Set route to auto-approve only when an invoice is not a duplicate, within tolerance, quantity-matched, and its vendor is on file; otherwise exception. Add a reason: clean match, price over tolerance, duplicate, vendor not in master, or missing receipt.
successMessage: Batch routed. One invoice auto-approves; four are sent to the exception queue with their reasons.
editorHelper: One row per invoice - route plus the reason it failed.

intro.heading: The fork: one clean path, one exception path

sections.title: Auto-approve is the strict path
sections.body: An invoice only takes the quiet path when it is clean on every check: not a duplicate, price within tolerance, quantity confirmed, and vendor on file. Miss any one and it becomes an exception.

sections.title: Every exception carries its reason
sections.body: Routing is not just a yes/no. Each held invoice is labeled with why it failed - price over tolerance, duplicate, vendor not in master, or missing receipt - so the right owner can work it without re-investigating.

sections.title: A duplicate always wins
sections.body: INV-58962 could have a perfect price and receipt and it would still route to exception, because it was already paid. The duplicate flag overrides everything else at the fork.

takeaway.heading: Batch routed at the fork
points: You applied one routing rule across the batch: auto-approve only when every check is clean.
INV-59001 took the auto-approve path; the other four were routed to exceptions.
Each exception carries its reason - price, duplicate, vendor, or receipt - so the right owner can act.
INV-58962 routed to exception on its duplicate flag alone, because a duplicate always wins.
The workflow can now split a mixed batch into a clean auto-approve path and a labeled exception path.
